newsitem.title: JAPAN: Intake blockage cuts Japan reactor output.
newsitem.headline: Intake blockage cuts Japan reactor output.

text.p: Chugoku Electric Power Co Inc was forced to temporarily cut its power output in half at its 820,000-kilowatt nuclear reactor in western Japan after a water cooling intake pump was blocked by a school of jellyfish, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

Operations of the two purifiers at the pump were automatically halted when jellyfish clogged them on Tuesday morning, forcing the utility firm to lower power production at the reactor to 440,000 kilowatts, a company spokesman said.
The utility started bringing operating rates back up again after removing the jellyfish, which took about 90 minutes.
The reactor is expected to reach full capacity by the end of the day, he said.
The spokesman also said that, although many jellyfish tend to be observed near the plant at this time of year, their numbers appear to be particularly heavy this year.
"This is the first time in 20 years we have had this many jellyfish," he said.
Chugoku is not at present considering any measures to keep jellyfish away from the reactor, as the probability of similar incidents recurring is likely to be extremely low, he said.
